model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of different algorithms in terms of accuracy (ACC) as a percentage, measured against the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and spans from 10^1 to 10^3, reflecting the co-occurrence count with a step size that corresponds to each algorithm's performance at varying co-occurrence numbers. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and ranges from 40 to 65, representing the accuracy percentage of the algorithms. The plot contains six lines, each representing a distinct algorithm with individual markers and line styles for identification: Base (circle markers connected by a solid line), MEND (diamond markers connected by a dashed line), FT (triangle up markers connected by a solid line), MEMIT (pentagon markers connected by a dotted line), IKE (arrow markers connected by a dash-dot line), and ROME (square markers connected by a solid line). The Base line remains relatively flat, showing little change in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. MEND starts just above 50% and shows a steep, consistent increase with higher co-occurrence numbers. FT begins around 45% and also increases as interaction frequency rises. MEMIT starts at just below 50%, with a steady climb, and ROME begins at the highest point, near 65%, and maintains a steady ascent throughout the range of co-occurrence counts.
